title: Moving Self-Referential Structs
pattern: Moving (by value assignment or swapping) a self-referential struct after it has constructed internal raw pointers to its own fields.
why_bad: Moving the struct changes its physical memory address. The internal pointers will continue to reference the old stack location, which is now invalid/garbage, leading to undefined behavior on dereference.
detection: A struct with fields containing pointers to other fields of the same struct is reassigned or moved without being wrapped in Pin.
counterexample: Using `Pin<&mut Self>` to guarantee that the self-referential struct can never be moved again in memory.
fix: Wrap the self-referential struct in `Pin`: `fn poll(self: Pin<&mut Self>)` to prevent compile-safe moves.
source: Rust For Rustaceans, Chapter 9 (Pin and Unpin) [456-457, 459].
